device.basis: Register block at 0xfff5b000 of X-T20 2.11 section 5. 0xca1970 reads +0x00 and 0xca1b98 writes +0x00, +0x04, +0x0c and +0x10 from the parameter block at 0x114be2c; no status bit, poll, interrupt or data move is known. The H.264 driver 0x15652c0..0x15663ec never references this page, so it is a separate register block, not a clock or gate for 0xfff5c000. The words read back their last write.

Playback display engine of X-T20 2.11 at 0xfffd5000. 0xc542d8 configures it and registers 0xc5421c for source 0x43 (descriptor row 0xed4a44, GIC line 0x8f = 143) with data 0x109f9b4. +0x000 bit 31 is ready and bit 0 starts a scanout; +0x008/+0x00c are the luma/chroma bases, +0x010 width, +0x014 pitch and +0x018 height in bits 16..31 (the stock path writes 1920, 1920 and 0x04400080 for a 1920x1088 frame). Completion status is +0x060 (bits 8/4/0), the mirror is +0x064, and +0x068 is final control; the handler reads +0x060, writes +0x064 and calls the queued callback, which posts 0x12c2. The 3-slot queue at 0x109f9b4 is guest RAM: byte +4 initialized, byte +5 running, word +0x0c slot count 3 and word +0x10 pending; 0xc54708/0xc54784 and the descriptor slots are guest writes, not modeled here. The job is one declared 100000-tick completion per start with status +0x064 bit 0 on IRQ 143; the real latency is not measured.

Movie image/H.264 front-end of X-T20 2.11 at 0xfff5c000 (driver 0x15652c0..0x15663ec; UniH264 wrappers 0x16b72d8/0x16b7318/0x16b74d8). The driver registers source 0x31 at 0x1565430; row 0x31 of table 0xed4720 is GIC line 0x6e (110). Input +0x100/+0x104/+0x108 are context +0x30/+0x38/+0x34 (0x184c9d0); output +0x01c/+0x028/+0x02c are context +0x04/+0x18/+0x1c through config +0x94/+0x98/+0x9c (0x184c8c4, 0x16b74d8, 0x1566200). The only writer of that context, 0x184c9d0, clears 0x44 bytes before storing the input pointers, so a stock recording presents 0/0/0; the model accepts a zero descriptor and keeps the frame in its diagnostic buffer. A non-zero descriptor keeps the model's declared +0x01c base and +0x028 end; +0x02c is stored only, and a base/end/next ring law is not witnessed. This node does not feed the MOV writer: the writer's stream descriptor is 0x1c26dfc {pointer, length, state, flag}, filled by codec callback 0x167aaf4 registered at 0x1bdd024 by 0x1554e30 (writer 0x167bff8). The codec library 0x1555xxx runs the 0xfffcc4xx window, reports the bitstream address at 0xfffcc4ac and sizes at 0xfffccd88/0xfffccd8c (source 0x3e, line 137), and the writer appends NALs at 0x167c354 with a 4-byte big-endian length at 0x167c50c..0x167c5ac. Framing is proved Annex B by parser 0x1553bc0..0x1554234 (00 00 00 01 start codes, SPS/PPS to 0x1a4fbc8/0x1a4fbac). Stock clips key every 60 samples, so GOP is 60. run_ticks 800000 is one 60 Hz frame in 48 MHz timer ticks (MOV rate table 0x167b69c maps selector 5 to 60; stock clips use 60000/1001); the encoder's completion latency within the frame is not measured.

Output 1 of the display controller, 0xfff64000-0xfff67000, as word registers that read back their last write. Two status laws from X-T20 2.11 seg5: 0xca37ac saves +0, writes bit 16, clears it and polls until bit 16 reads set before restoring the saved word with bit 16; 0xca9df0 sets bit 28 of +0x2000 and polls until it reads clear. Both requests complete at once; the controller's real latency (likely one frame) is not measured. Output 0 at 0xfff59000 follows the same bit-16 law in 0xca37ac but is not exercised up to REC and is not declared. Scanout: the commit routine 0xca5a0c copies its shadow block to the OSD layer group (+0x200 layer enable bits; four origins +0x210, sizes +0x220 and buffers +0x230). Camera RAM (live-service reads 2026-10-29) holds the same layer as enable 1, size 0x2cf01df and buffer 0x384d000 in REC and 0x354d000 in the menu, with 720 x 480 premultiplied RGBA buffers at a 2880-byte pitch. The same routine copies the video layer: format +0x010, size +0x02c, buffer +0x030. Camera REC holds format 0x333 (packed 4:2:2 Y0 Y1 Cb Cr, 720 x 480) with the live-view buffer 0xa7d6000 and control word +0 = 0x1010105; the emulated firmware writes 0x1010101 before REC and 0x1010105 on entering REC while +0x030 cycles through the live-view buffers, so +0 bit 2 is the video enable. The output is captured as host output 0 (the rear panel) at the frame period: OSD layers over the video layer when bit 2 is set, otherwise over black. The video conversion is BT.601 limited range (the shared raster law, not measured) and keeps the OSD buffers' blue-first byte order. X-T20 2.11 takes each OSD window's enable from its nibble of output register +0x20c, with the row skip at +0x320 and the blend law of the format selector; with that window model, Focal pages (720 pixels in a 1024-pixel row, straight A,B,G,R) and stock overlays match the reference emulator byte for byte.
device.frame_basis: Frame interrupts of the display controller, as an interrupt law without its registers. Seg5 source table 0xed4720 rows 73-78 connect lines 112-114 and 117-119 (edge) to handlers that run the callbacks queued by 0xc9dc38 for output 0 or 1 and event 0-2 (0xc9d854, 0xc9d994); the handlers read no controller register. The X-T20 2.11 vglib thread clears bit 16 of 0xfff65000 or 0xfff5a000, queues such a callback and yields at priority 7 until it runs (0xcad290), which starves flashload before section 7 loads. The period is an assumed 60 Hz in 48 MHz timer ticks (the 10 ms system tick reloads 480000); the panel rate is not measured.

device.basis: Output 0 of the X-T20 display controller at 0xfff59000. The register window covers the output-0 accesses in X-T20 2.11, with the highest observed offset +0xc0c (0xca29c8); the separate body register block at 0xfff5b000 is outside this window. The stock output-0 path waits for bit 16 at +0 to read set (0xca37ac). No output-0 bit-28 status at +0x2000 is modeled. Status requests complete immediately; controller latency is not measured. Registers start at their default values and change only through firmware MMIO, so this path remains inactive until firmware programs it. Scanout is attached to host output 1 to observe it separately; physical panel identity and panel-specific color behavior are unchecked. X-T20 2.11 takes each OSD window's enable from its nibble of output register +0x20c, with the row skip at +0x320 and the blend law of the format selector; with that window model, Focal pages (720 pixels in a 1024-pixel row, straight A,B,G,R) and stock overlays match the reference emulator byte for byte.

DMP SMAPH vector-graphics renderer with the XP4 register interface. The X-T20 2.11 OpenVG/EGL driver (seg5 0xdda65c onward, kernel tasks smaphk/smaphp) programs command words at +0x1c, the copy unit at +0xc00-+0xc18 (initialization 0xdda748 sets +0xc1c to 0x8000) and command lists at +0x10d0/+0x10e0. Its interrupt 92 handler 0xdda2fc reads status +0x34, and waiter 0xdda3cc reports bits 31, 30 and 26. On X-T20 2.11 an equal-shape copy keeps each pixel word (A,B,G,R bytes), as the reference emulator's renderer does; Focal pages exported through the copy engine then match it byte for byte.

xt20-discovery.dram_basis: Camera MMU first-level table (X-T20 2.11, ff80 read of 0x108000, 2026-10-20): virtual 0-0x3fffffff is normal memory over physical 0. The second bank at 0x80000000 is not declared; no RAM population was measured.
limits: Command-dial edge pacing comes from the emulator, not from camera measurement: on the stock REC X-T20 2.11 graph board the dial poller 0xc8f440 runs every 120000 board ticks (2.5 ms at 48 MHz; 13 entries over 6M executed instructions, deltas 115447..124850, median 119945), and it posts a step after one stable poll (descriptor field +0x14 = 1 at 0xf7a584), so each declared phase edge is held for 240000 ticks, two poll periods.

One firmware step is one full Gray cycle (0xc8fb80 forms 2*A+B from bank 1 bits 2/3 and 4/5; table 0xf7a668 front, 0xf7a64c rear posts 0x25/0x3d for 0->1 and 0x24/0x3c for 1->0). Edges per physical detent are not measured, so the model steps in firmware steps and claims no detent count.
The declared rest phase 2 (A high, B low) is the power-on GPIO bank 1 word 0x1014; one capture held bits 3/5 high instead, so the dial's physical rest position is not established.
